mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, observed over the last two weeks (from -18.0% to -13.6%), indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an increase compared to the mean of the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained high and increasing level of GROCERY_PHARM mobility, reaching over 20% above baseline (22.4% at t-0w), suggests a general increase in out-of-home activity that will spill over into retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above 20% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both PARKS and TRANSIT mobility (both showing recent upward trends) indicates a broader public willingness to engage in outdoor and public space activities, which will translate into increased foot traffic for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If both PARKS and TRANSIT mobility increase, but RETAIL_REC does not show a positive change over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility, falling below -20% (currently -21.9% at t-0w) and continuing to decline, suggests a shift towards more remote work or reduced office presence, which typically correlates with reduced weekday retail activity and will drive RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20% and continues to decline week-on-week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility falls below -20% and continues to decline, but RETAIL_REC does not decrease over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The stable and slightly elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (around 6-7% above baseline) suggests that a significant portion of the population continues to spend more time at home, limiting the potential for a strong rebound in RETAIL_REC, thus keeping it relatively stable or slightly negative over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains stable, but RETAIL_REC shows a significant positive increase over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The recent strong recovery in TRANSIT mobility, moving from -9.7% to -7.4% in the last week (a 2.3 percentage point increase), indicates increasing comfort with public transport and a return to out-of-home activities, which will boost RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high GROCERY_PHARM mobility (22.4% at t-0w) and stable RESIDENTIAL mobility (6.6% at t-0w) suggests that while essential outings are common, people are not yet fully returning to non-essential activities, which will temper RETAIL_REC growth and keep it relatively flat or slightly negative over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains high and RESIDENTIAL stable, but RETAIL_REC shows a significant positive increase over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent recovery in PARKS mobility, showing week-on-week increases for the last three weeks (-27.4 to -22.0%), indicates improving weather or public confidence in outdoor activities, which often precedes or coincides with increased retail and recreation spending, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS shows a consistent week-on-week increase for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility consistently increases for three weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days.
